 This position is in the Logic Technology Development (LTD) team, working in one of the most advanced semiconductor development facilities in the world.
   

  

 The LTD Resolution Enhancement Technology (RET) team is extending the limits of feature sizes that are patternable on Intel's devices, using current and future lithography manufacturing tooling. The team works closely with fab integrated lithography process and mask manufacturing teams using computational lithography tooling to optimize mask patterns and maximize manufacturing process capability. The RET team also works closely with the design rule definition teams, using lithography and patterning simulation capabilities to determine design rules for future Intel process nodes.

* Optical Proximity Correction (OPC) simulations
* Research, development, and implementation of Resolution Enhancement Techniques (RET) for existing and novel process technologies
* Defines and selects new approaches and implementation of RET
* Maintains substantial knowledge of the state\-of\-the\-art principles and theories in lithography, optics, photoresists, computer modeling, and software engineering
* Image processing and statistical analysis of data for OPC models
* OPC model calibration
* OPC recipe code optimization and validation
* Algorithmic design pattern layout manipulation
* Use predictive modeling, statistics, machine learning, and other data analysis techniques to collect, explore, visualize fab process data, and develop RET software algorithms and applications to compensate for physical effects in photolithography imaging and the etch pattern transfer process
* Support of production mask tapeout and RET validation
* Maintain a deep knowledge of state\-of\-the\-art principles and trends in RET and semiconductor technology
* Creation of technical documentation and presentations

 VTG is seeking an experienced, mid\-career full\-stack software engineer to lead technical execution on assigned projects. This role owns significant design and architecture decisions at the intersection of data engineering, full\-stack development, and mission analytics, with direct impact on national security and industrial base resilience. You will operate as a senior technical contributor in an agile product environment, driving the architecture of a modern web\-based platform that integrates diverse data sources, applies risk scoring across DoD taxonomies, and delivers actionable insights to senior defense stakeholders. This role is expected to mentor junior developers and partner directly with government stakeholders on technical direction.
   

  

**What will you do?**
* Architect, design, and lead development of full\-stack features
* Own front\-end architecture using React, establishing patterns and standards for intuitive, data\-rich user experiences
* Design and build scalable backend services and APIs using Python
* Lead integration of structured and unstructured data sources to support supply chain risk analytics
* Drive technical planning within an Agile/Scrum team, including sprint planning, backlog grooming, and story estimation using Jira
* Establish and enforce code quality standards, conduct code reviews, and maintain CI/CD pipelines using GitLab
* Lead data modeling and visualization efforts aligned to DoD risk taxonomies
* Serve as a technical lead in requirements refinement, sprint planning, and architecture/design discussions with government stakeholders
* Own documentation required for Risk Management Framework (RMF) alignment and auditability
* Mentor junior and mid\-level developers, providing technical guidance and code review feedback
* Identify technical risks and propose mitigation strategies to program leadership
* Develop and execute Software Test Plans (STPs) and associated test cases covering unit, integration, system, and regression testing
* Perform functional and regression testing to validate new features and confirm defect fixes prior to release
* Support debugging and root cause analysis (RCA) of defects identified during testing, staging, or production, partnering with QA and government stakeholders through resolution and closure
* Document test results, defect reports, and requirements traceability matrices (RTM) to support test readiness reviews and RMF/audit requirements

 You are a seasoned, technically strong engineer who has shipped production software end\-to\-end and is ready to take ownership of architecture and technical direction. * Experience with test automation frameworks (e.g., Selenium, Cypress, PyTest) and CI/CD\-integrated automated regression suites

**About The Role**
 As Codex adoption grows inside large organizations, customers are increasingly trusting Codex with their most valuable assets: proprietary codebases, internal documentation, customer data, and sensitive workflows.
   

  

 This role will help build the enterprise control plane that makes Codex secure, governable, and trustworthy at scale. You will design and operate backend systems that give enterprise administrators visibility and control over how Codex is used across their organization.
   

  

 You will work across identity, access, encryption, policy enforcement, auditability, and admin controls. This may include systems that let customers manage encryption keys, control which Codex capabilities are enabled, enforce organizational policies, and understand how data flows through Codex.
   

  

 This role owns systems end\-to\-end: from architecture and implementation to production operations, with a strong bias for security, reliability, quality, and velocity.
   

  

**In This Role, You Will**
* Build backend systems that protect enterprise customer data, including encryption, key management, access controls, data isolation, retention controls, and secure data handling patterns.
* Design and operate the Codex enterprise control plane, enabling administrators to configure, enforce, and audit how Codex is used across users, teams, projects, and environments.
* Build policy and governance systems that allow enterprises to enable or disable specific Codex capabilities, define organizational constraints, and safely roll out new AI\-powered workflows.
* Develop reliable, observable, and scalable services across identity, authorization, configuration, audit logging, compliance, and enterprise administration.
* Partner closely with product, security, infrastructure, GTM, and customer\-facing teams to translate complex enterprise requirements into simple, durable product and platform capabilities.
* Help define what “enterprise\-grade” means for AI software engineering systems as Codex becomes a trusted teammate inside the world’s largest organizations.


**You Might Thrive In This Role If You**
* Have strong backend software engineering fundamentals and experience building production\-grade distributed systems.
* Are proficient in one or more backend languages such as Python, Go, Rust, Java, or C\+\+.
* Have experience with security, identity, authorization, encryption, key management, policy systems, or enterprise governance.
* Understand enterprise foundations such as SSO/SAML/OIDC, SCIM, RBAC, audit logging, compliance controls, and data governance.
* Enjoy building foundational platform capabilities that unlock many product surfaces and customer workflows.
* Are comfortable working across ambiguous technical and product requirements, especially in fast\-moving 0 → 1 environments.
* Care deeply about reliability, security, observability, and customer trust.

**Company Overview**
 Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion\-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real\-time APIs for speech\-to\-text (STT), text\-to\-speech (TTS), and building production\-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300\+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice\-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self\-hosted and on\-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.
   

  

****Company Operating Rhythm****
 At Deepgram, we expect an AI\-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.
   

  

 Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.
   

  

 Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day\-to\-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9\-to\-5\.
   

  

****The Opportunity****
 Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real\-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.
   

  

****The Role****
 Deepgram is seeking a highly skilled and versatile Machine Learning Engineer to join our Research team. As a Member of the Research Staff, you will partner with research scientists to prototype and validate novel modeling ideas, then scale them through robust training systems for speech technologies, internal tooling, and innovative data strategies. You'll work at the intersection of machine learning, data infrastructure, and internal tooling to support our mission of building world\-class speech recognition and synthesis systems. On the Research team, you will experiment with new technologies and techniques, while also working on product\-focused deliverables, learning from colleagues with a wide range of expertise in AI and machine learning as you go.
   

  

****Key Responsibilities****
* Scalable Model Training: Architect and manage horizontally scalable systems that dramatically accelerate the end\-to\-end training lifecycle for Speech\-to\-Text (STT) and Text\-to\-Speech (TTS) models. This includes far more than automated training: the role focuses on making model development significantly faster and more efficient through optimized data preparation and management, high\-throughput training pipelines, distributed infrastructure, and automated evaluation tooling.
* Tooling \& Accessibility: Design and implement internal UIs and tools that make ML systems and workflows accessible to non\-technical stakeholders across the company. These UIs should be designed to provide transparency and flexibility to internally built tooling.
* Infrastructure \& Tools: Oversee and manage training tooling, job orchestration, experiment tracking, and data storage.


****The Challenge****
 We are seeking Members of the Research Staff who:
   

  

* See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches
* Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months
* Have the vision to scale successful proofs\-of\-concept 100x
* Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact


 If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative.
   

  

****It's Important to Us That You Have****
* Strong experience with the machine learning research pipeline, particularly in STT or related speech domains. This includes experimenting with and evaluating new architectures and modeling approaches, and implementing large\-scale training systems.
* Proficiency with orchestration and infrastructure tools like Kubernetes, Docker, and Prefect.
* Familiarity with ML lifecycle tools such as MLflow.
* Experience building internal tools or dashboards for non\-technical users.
* Hands\-on experience with data engineering practices for unstructured audio and text data.
* Comfortable working in cross\-functional teams that include researchers, engineers, and product stakeholders.


****Why Join Deepgram?****
 At Deepgram, you’ll help shape the future of human–machine communication. Our research culture prioritizes ownership, experimentation, and real\-world impact. As a Member of the Research Staff, you'll be empowered to build tools and systems that accelerate ML research and product deployment at scale.

Founding Data Scientist: Measurement, Psychometrics \& the FSU Career Profile Future State University (FSU)
 



  





 About FSU We're building an AI\-native applied learning platform: a 3D simulation engine that converts any syllabus or training doc into immersive, decision\-based career simulations. Fortnite\-meets\-LinkedIn for education. But under the hood, FSU is a measurement system that happens to run as a game. Every decision a learner makes inside a sim becomes scored, traceable evidence of what they can actually do, and that evidence rolls up into the FSU Career Profile: a new kind of resume, built from behavior, not test scores.
 



  





 The Role We're hiring a Founding Data Scientist to own that measurement system end to end. You are equal parts measurement scientist and data/ML engineer: you build the models that turn behavior into scores, and you prove those scores are valid. This is the person who makes FSU's core claim true, that a number on a Career Profile means what we say it means, and would survive a skeptical psychometrician.
 



  





 This is hands\-on and foundational. You will design the scoring architecture, build the evidence pipeline, validate it against real psychometric standards, co\-validate it with our academic research partners, and stand up the dashboards that make all of it legible to students, instructors, and us. You build the measurement, and you build the system that produces it.
 



 If you've built assessment or scoring models, you think in constructs, validity, and reliability, and you can ship the engineering yourself, read on.
 



  





 What You'll Own
 


* The scoring architecture: an evidence\-centered design pipeline (Mislevy\-style) that turns every gradeable moment into typed, routed, provenance\-backed evidence. The append\-only event spine and the per\-learner mastery model that is the single source of truth for every score.
* Validity and reliability: content validity by construction (constructs anchored to learning objectives), discriminant validity (proving our dimensions measure distinct things, not the same thing five times), and inter\-rater reliability between our LLM raters and human experts. You own the evidence that our measurement holds up.
* Knowledge tracing: per\-concept mastery estimation (BKT and beyond) from decisions graded against authored answer keys.
* Behavioral measurement: estimating durable skills, professional identity, values, and epistemology from behavior in simulations, each with confidence, recency, and a traceable chain back to the exact moment that produced the number.
* The FSU Career Profile: the read model behind our credential. You turn the mastery model into the profile employers and learners trust, verified by doing, with provenance behind every claim.
* LLM\-as\-rater systems: rubric design, prompt versioning, eval sets, and the stability and audit tooling that keeps a model\-graded score defensible.
* Internal analytics for all three audiences: student engagement and at\-risk detection, instructor class\-insight dashboards, and an internal observability and watchdog view (latency, errors, cost\-per\-session, model drift) across the full stack.
* Co\-validation with our academic partners: working alongside published researchers to independently validate the instrument.
* Recruiting, mentoring, and building the data team beneath you as we scale.



  





 What You Bring
 


* Serious data science and ML engineering chops. You build production models in Python and ship them; you are not just analyzing in a notebook.
* Real grounding in measurement: psychometrics, educational measurement, or assessment science. Validity, reliability, construct modeling, IRT, BKT, or evidence\-centered design. You have built something that had to measure a person fairly.
* Fluency with LLMs as measurement instruments: eval design, LLM\-as\-judge, and the discipline to know when a model's score is trustworthy and when it isn't.
* Enough full\-stack range to stand up your own dashboards and wire read models into a product. You don't wait on someone else to make your work visible.
* Startup\-native: hands\-on, fast, and comfortable owning an ambiguous, foundational problem from scratch.
* Clear thinking about data. You know the difference between pulling a number and knowing whether it's any good, and you can explain a validity argument to someone who isn't a statistician.



  





 Bonus
 


* Published or applied work in educational measurement, learning analytics, or game\-based assessment.
* Knowledge tracing, IRT, or Bayesian modeling in production.
* Simulation, serious\-games, or EdTech background.
* MongoDB, LangChain / LangSmith, or LLM\-eval tooling in your stack.
* You've built a credential, a score, or a rating that other people relied on to make real decisions.



  





 Why Join FSU Own the measurement system behind a genuinely new credential, the thing that decides whether "verified by doing" is real or just marketing. This is a rare problem: measuring what people can actually do, from behavior, with the rigor to defend it and the AI tooling to do it at scale. Greenfield architecture, real academic co\-validation, high equity, real ownership, and a world\-class mission\-driven team.
